items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, punchy, urgent and surprised in the opening question, like a scroll-stopping opener, with a clear pause after it, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline; quieter and serious for the line about the invasion and fighting. Chars voices a funny deadpan cartoon character (a talking line on a map), short and dry.
lines: Did you know... North Korea and South Korea are still at war?
The shooting stopped in nineteen fifty-three... but the war never ended.
It all started with a border drawn in one night... on a magazine map.
It's nineteen forty-five. Japan has lost World War Two... and Korea with it.
Soviet troops pour in from the north. The Americans? About six hundred miles away.
Late at night, two U.S. officers look for a line... north of Seoul.
No river. No mountains. Just a number: the thirty-eighth parallel.
[deadpan, mildly offended, dry and slow] Me? I'm literally just a latitude.
It was meant to be temporary. Spoiler... it wasn't.
So how did a latitude become a war that won't end?
By nineteen forty-eight, each half had its own government... claiming the whole peninsula.
In nineteen fifty, the North invaded. Three years of war followed.
Peace talks dragged on for two years... and one hundred and fifty-eight meetings.
And you thought your office meetings were long.
In July nineteen fifty-three, they finally signed... an armistice.
That's a ceasefire. A pause button. Not a peace treaty.
And South Korea? It never even signed.
In nineteen fifty-four, peace talks in Geneva... failed.
So the guns went quiet... but the war never officially ended.
This August, Seoul asked again to end it. So far... no treaty.
The ceasefire line became the D-M-Z: about two hundred and forty kilometres long, roughly Delhi to Jaipur, and just four kilometres wide.
With almost no people inside, wildlife moved in: over six thousand species.
[deadpan, tired, sarcastic sigh] Temporary... they said.
Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
